round: the tester's fail on AC2 — `bun x biome` and `npx biome` reach the same squatted package and passed the gate

proof.criterion: AC2, the tester's failure — the required lint job fails if the vulnerable form reappears, in every spelling that reaches a package runner.
proof.surface: This role container (worker image, bun 1.3.14, workspace with no node_modules) for the defect itself; `.github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh` on the real tree, its own 78-case suite, and a fixture built as that suite builds them (the real script symlinked into a miniature repository) for the gate.
proof.command: bun x biome check . ; bun x biome --version ; npx biome check . ; npx biome --version ; then PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh and .test.sh ; then the same guard against a fixture holding `bun x biome check .` and `npx biome check .` in a fenced AGENTS.md block, `npm exec -- tsc --noEmit` in a .sh and `yarn dlx biome check src/` in a recipe
proof.observed: The defect reproduces at this head: `bun x biome check .` and `npx biome check .` each exit 0 having printed nothing and checked no file, and both `--version` answers are 0.3.3 — the squatted package, not the Biome 2.4.11 bun.lock pins. The gate now refuses the whole package-runner family by basename (bunx, pnpx, npx, and the two-word bun x, npm exec, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx) and refuses a command it cannot read (a segment an unexpanded expansion begins that names a pinned tool). The tree passes — `every prescribed biome, tsc, tsserver and playwright command runs through scripts/repo-tool.sh (13 manifest(s), 8 workflow(s), 92 shell script(s), 551 guide(s))`, exit 0 — and the suite reports `Results: 78 passed, 0 failed`, the tester's three red cases among them, their text unmodified (the file's diff removes no line).
proof.negativeControl: The fixture above fails with exit 1 naming all four at their own lines (`packages/thing/package.json:4` yarn dlx, `scripts/x.sh:2` npm exec, `AGENTS.md:4` bun x, `AGENTS.md:5` npx), and `bun run lint`, `bun test`, `bun build` and `npm view` still pass, so the resolver table did not swallow the ordinary commands. The tree's own files were never edited for either run.

proof.criterion: AC2's coverage gap the tester recorded as an observation — fifteen nested AGENTS.md and README.md files were matched by none of the guard's patterns, so a prescribed command written in one would pass unjudged.
proof.surface: The guard's own tree walk over this repository, and a fixture carrying a nested guide.
proof.command: PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh (its printed counts), and a fixture whose packages/envoy/infra/AGENTS.md fenced block holds `bunx biome check .`
proof.observed: The guide set is now every AGENTS.md and every README.md at any depth, outside the excluded directories, with the rest of the set unchanged: the count rises from 536 to 551 and the tree still passes. The fifteen newly judged files are deploy/kubernetes/operator-route/README.md, docs/site/media/broker/README.md and walkthrough/README.md, packages/contracts/fixtures/classification/README.md, packages/envoy's cmd/agent-secrets, cmd/broker, cmd/dispatch (README and AGENTS), deploy, infra (README and AGENTS) and scripts READMEs, packages/pi-envoy/scripts/README.md, scripts/dispatch/README.md and scripts/e2e/README.md; none of them prescribed a vulnerable command, so none needed fixing.
proof.negativeControl: The nested-guide fixture fails at the line inside its block; before this change the same fixture passed, which is the hole the tester named.

proof.criterion: The architect's ruling on the tester's lock-wait observation — the whole script stays inside one start budget, and no wait inside it can expire before the thing it waits for.
proof.surface: The throwaway copy of this tree on the issue volume (/legion/workspaces/infra-71-proof), with a second process holding /usr/bin/flock on the cache directory, and the script's own 114-case suite against a stub bun.
proof.command: /usr/bin/flock -w 60 /legion/bun/cache sleep 30 & then env … LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=2 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh, timed ; env … LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=1 sh scripts/legion-setup.sh against a 33 s install ; bash scripts/legion-setup.test.sh
proof.observed: One bound now: LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET (270 s by default, the two old numbers' sum), and every wait inside it — the flock on the cache, the install's timeout, the retry — is what is left of it when that wait begins, the install's own computed under the lock so two waits cannot add past the whole. Against a 30 s holder with a 2 s budget the run exits 0 after 2 s measured, with `another install held /legion/bun/cache for this run's whole 2s budget`, reason lock-timeout, exitStatus 199, no marker. A 1 s budget against a 33 s install is install-timeout, 124. The suite reports `Results: 114 passed, 0 failed`. Worst case is the budget plus the 5 s `timeout` leaves between SIGTERM and SIGKILL: 275 s inside the 360 s registration deadline.
proof.negativeControl: LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_WAIT and LEGION_SETUP_INSTALL_TIMEOUT no longer exist anywhere outside the committed handoffs (grep), so no caller can set a lock wait smaller than the install it waits for; and the cold-race stub with a budget too small for a second attempt runs once and reports the failure rather than retrying past the budget.

proof.criterion: AC1 — in a role container where the repository's packages are not installed, no command the repository tells an agent to run reports a passing lint.
proof.surface: This role container, $LEGION_WORKSPACE with no node_modules, poisoned by one `bunx biome check .`.
proof.command: bun run lint packages/pi-legion/ ; bun run typecheck ; (cd packages/pi-legion && bun run lint) ; scripts/repo-tool.sh biome check .
proof.observed: Each exits 1 with the wrapper's message naming the tool, both paths tried and the remedy. Unchanged by this round, re-run at its head.
proof.negativeControl: In the same container `bunx biome check .`, `bun x biome check .` and `npx biome check .` each exit 0 having checked nothing, every `--version` answering 0.3.3.

proof.criterion: AC3, AC4's agent half and AC5 — the install, the report and the second role, re-driven at this head because the setup script changed.
proof.surface: The throwaway copy on the issue volume, run through the deployment's own argv, and a real Oh My Pi pane (LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp, runLegionPane).
proof.command: sh scripts/legion-setup.sh cold ; ./node_modules/.bin/biome --version ; bun run lint . ; cksum bun.lock ; find /tmp $HOME -newer <marker> ; a second run as another role ; BUN_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:1/ with nothing cached ; bun test on a throwaway runLegionPane case
proof.observed: Exit 0 after `1986 packages installed [32.99s]`; biome 2.4.11 and `Checked 1079 files in 35s`; `cksum bun.lock` 581893351 340936 before and after; no report; the container's own disk took one 0-byte /tmp/.<hex>-00000000.hm and nothing else ($HOME/.bun 113086919 and $HOME/.cache/bun 1605253 before and after). The second role: `already installed; nothing to do` in 0.036 s, the cache byte-identical (1395623403), 0 files newer than the marker. An unreachable registry: exit 0, install-failed, 1, 999-character detail, no marker, and the next successful run clears the report. The real pane carries the notice for its own issue, role and generation.
proof.negativeControl: `bun run lint .` in that copy before the install exits 1 with the wrapper's message; the pane whose report names generation 9 carries no notice (2 pass, 0 fail); removing node_modules/.bin/biome makes the next run install again.

filesChanged: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh: the package-runner family by basename (bunx, pnpx, npx; bun x, npm exec, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx), a fail-closed rule for a segment an unexpanded expansion begins that names a pinned tool, and a guide set of every AGENTS.md and README.md at any depth.

.github/scripts/check-check-commands.test.sh: additions only — every new spelling in a judged context, the unreadable-command rule with its two negatives, a nested-guide case, and a negative that bun run/bun test/bun build/npm view still pass. The tester's three red cases are untouched and pass.

scripts/legion-setup.sh and scripts/legion-setup.test.sh: one LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET for the whole run, every wait inside it taken from what remains (the install's computed under the lock), and the marker's comment naming what it is keyed by and what production guarantees about it.
docs/kubernetes.md: the setup section's bounds paragraph, rewritten for the one budget and its worst case.
trickyParts: `timeout`'s duration is fixed when its argument is expanded, so an install handed what was left when the flock *started* would be given a budget the wait had since spent. The install's bound is therefore computed by the shell flock runs, after the lock is taken.
The gate reads a word as it was written rather than after stripping a leading `$`, so an expansion-led command stays whole for the fail-closed rule; a prompt's `$ ` in a guide is still stepped over.

The workspace is still deliberately without node_modules: AC1's state is the uninstalled one and every later role of this issue mounts this workspace. Every install proof ran in /legion/workspaces/infra-71-proof, removed at the end of the phase.
deviations: The architect asked for the principle rather than two strings, so the gate covers `pnpm dlx` and `yarn dlx` although no image installs either today, and refuses a shape it cannot read instead of passing it.

LEGION_SETUP_LOCK_WAIT and LEGION_SETUP_INSTALL_TIMEOUT are gone rather than kept beside the new budget: two conventions for one bound is what produced the defect the tester observed. Nothing outside this repository set them.
openQuestions: Unchanged from the first round: AC3's full line, AC4's daemon half and AC5's two-role form are production-check criteria and need the worker image pin and the one `runtime.kubernetes.setup` line, which must name none of the runtime-owned variables (BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR, TMPDIR, GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE, XDG_CACHE_HOME).

The tester's fourth observation is not this change's: packages/pi-legion/extensions/legion-role-tools-omp.test.ts passes against a partially installed node_modules, where neither plugin entry loads. It is outside this diff and is left for the architect to route.
discoveredComplexity: The image ships npm and npx beside bun, so a resolver this repository never uses is one word away from any agent's keyboard; the gate's rule has to be the family, not the spelling the guide happens to use.
Fifteen guides lived outside the gate's patterns. A set written as an enumeration of paths drifts as the tree grows; `**/AGENTS.md` and `**/README.md` cannot.
